prompt.adult: Paul ends his long discussion of Israel and the nations with praise. What does he exclaim over in 11:33, “both of the wisdom and knowledge of God”?
prompt.child: At the end of Romans 11, Paul bursts into praise for God’s wisdom. What does he say “Oh” about?
prompt.older: According to Romans 11:33, what does Paul exclaim over?

verses.text: Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments and His ways past finding out!

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 33.
explanation.teen: 11:33 opens with an exclamation, then speaks of His judgments and ways. Read the opening.

teaching.extended_explanation: 11:33 goes on, “How unsearchable are His judgments and His ways past finding out!”
teaching.takeaway: Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God!

prompt.adult: According to 11:29, what are the gifts and the calling of God?
prompt.child: Paul says something about God’s gifts and His calling. What does he say they are?
prompt.teen: Romans 11:29: “For the gifts and the calling of God are” what?
prompt.older: What word does Romans 11:29 use for the gifts and calling of God?

verses.text: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

explanation.child: Look at the very end of verse 29.
explanation.teen: 11:29 names the gifts and the calling, then describes them. Read the description.
explanation.older: It follows “the calling of God are” in 11:29.

teaching.extended_explanation: 11:28 says they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
teaching.takeaway: The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

prompt.adult: Paul asks whether Israel stumbled that they should fall, and says, “Certainly not!” According to 11:11, why has salvation come to the Gentiles?
prompt.child: Paul says salvation came to the Gentiles because of Israel’s fall. What purpose does he give for it?
prompt.teen: Romans 11:11: “But through their fall,” for what purpose “salvation has come to the Gentiles”?
prompt.older: According to Romans 11:11, for what purpose has salvation come to the Gentiles through Israel’s fall?

choices.text: to keep the nations far away
to end the promise to Israel

verses.text: I say then, have they stumbled that they should fall? Certainly not! But through their fall, to provoke them to jealousy, salvation has come to the Gentiles.
Now if their fall is riches for the world, and their failure riches for the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!

explanation.adult: Read the middle of the last sentence of 11:11.
explanation.child: Look between “through their fall” and “salvation” in verse 11.
explanation.teen: 11:11 asks a question, answers it, and then gives a purpose. Read the purpose.
explanation.older: It follows “But through their fall” in 11:11.

teaching.extended_explanation: 11:12 says their fall is riches for the world, and asks, “how much more their fullness!”
teaching.takeaway: Through their fall, to provoke them to jealousy, salvation has come to the Gentiles.

prompt.adult: Paul prays that Israel may be saved. In 10:2, what does he bear witness that they have for God, though not according to knowledge?
prompt.child: Paul bears witness about his people in 10:2. What does he say they have for God?
prompt.teen: Romans 10:2: “For I bear them witness that they have” what “for God”?
prompt.older: According to Romans 10:2, what does Israel have for God?

verses.text: Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is that they may be saved.
For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

explanation.teen: 10:1 is Paul’s prayer; 10:2 gives what they have, then what it lacks. Read what they have.
explanation.older: It follows “witness that they have” in 10:2.

teaching.extended_explanation: 10:1 calls it his heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel. 10:2 adds, “but not according to knowledge.”
teaching.takeaway: They have a zeal for God.

prompt.adult: In 9:2, what does Paul say he has in his heart, as he thinks of his countrymen according to the flesh?
prompt.child: Paul writes about how he feels for his own people. What does he say is in his heart?
prompt.teen: Romans 9:2: “that I have” what “in my heart”?
prompt.older: According to Romans 9:2, what does Paul carry in his heart for his brethren?

choices.text: deep shame and a lasting regret

verses.text: that I have great sorrow and continual grief in my heart.
For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my countrymen according to the flesh,

explanation.child: Look at the words of verse 2.
explanation.teen: 9:2 names what he has; 9:3 tells what he could wish for their sake. Read 9:2.

teaching.extended_explanation: 9:3 says he could wish himself accursed from Christ for his brethren.
teaching.takeaway: I have great sorrow and continual grief in my heart.

prompt.adult: In 9:22 Paul speaks of God’s much longsuffering. In 11:22, what does he say God shows on those who fell?
prompt.child: Paul tells his readers to think about two sides of God. What does God show toward those who fell?
prompt.older: Linking Romans 9:22 with 11:22, what is shown on those who fell?

verses.text: What if God, wanting to show His wrath and to make His power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction,
Therefore consider the goodness and severity of God: on those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in His goodness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.

explanation.adult: Read the words after the colon in 11:22.
explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 11:22.
explanation.teen: 9:22 is the setting; 11:22 names two things, then says on whom each is shown. Read the first of these.
explanation.older: It follows “on those who fell,” in 11:22.

teaching.extended_explanation: 9:22 says God endured the vessels of wrath. 11:22 warns, “Otherwise you also will be cut off.”

prompt.adult: In 9:20 Paul asks, “who are you to reply against God?” In 11:34, what has no one become to the LORD?
prompt.child: Paul asks who has known the mind of the LORD. What else does he ask whether anyone has become?
prompt.older: Alongside 9:20, what does 11:34 say no one has become to the LORD?

verses.text: But indeed, O man, who are you to reply against God? Will the thing formed say to him who formed it, “Why have you made me like this?”
“For who has known the mind of the LORD? Or who has become His counselor?”

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 34.
explanation.teen: 9:20 is the setting; 11:34 asks two questions. Read the second.
explanation.older: It follows “Or who has become” in 11:34.

teaching.extended_explanation: 9:20 asks whether the thing formed may say to him who formed it, “Why have you made me like this?” 11:34 first asks who has known the mind of the LORD.

prompt.adult: In 10:15 Paul asks how they shall preach unless they are sent. In 11:13, what does he call himself?
prompt.child: Paul tells his readers in Rome what God sent him to be. What does he call himself?
prompt.older: Linking Romans 10:15 with 11:13, what does Paul call himself?

choices.text: a servant of the high priest

verses.text: And how shall they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the gospel of peace, Who bring glad tidings of good things!”
For I speak to you Gentiles; inasmuch as I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry,

explanation.child: Look after “inasmuch as I am” in verse 13.
explanation.teen: 10:15 asks about those who are sent; 11:13 says whom he speaks to, then what he is. Read what he is.
explanation.older: It follows “inasmuch as I am” in 11:13.

teaching.extended_explanation: 10:15 quotes Isaiah about the beautiful feet of those who bring glad tidings. 11:13 ends, “I magnify my ministry.”
teaching.takeaway: I am an apostle to the Gentiles.
